title: Bond distance on knot trees: what is proved
claim: On every knot tree of parity, not-all-equal and betweenness knots, in any mixture, bond distance (least bond holding both, minus one) is steps apart plus one on every pair: upper bound by the bond {x, y, third distinction of each path knot}; lower bound, for any three-place knots passing K2, because a bond missing a path knot's third branch projects as a product. Equality fails for the clause 'not all ones' (no bond holds a chain's ends). On the mixed cycle (NAE path closed by a parity knot) bond distance reads the parity knot as one knot. Bond distance has no hub shortcut. Refereed R1: the forcing of U works knot by knot for each of the six laws (not by one global switch); bond distance satisfies the triangle inequality on parity bases (the referee's proof) and knot trees, not on every base.
standard_statement: Bonds are the minimal non-shattered sets of the family of allowed states (Sauer-Shelah, Pajor); the product lemma is the acyclic join-tree decomposition (Beeri, Fagin, Maier and Yannakakis 1983; Freuder 1982); on parity bases bonds are matroid circuits.
